tonight.headline: Thursday night went against you: Furia Regia lead 41.5 to 0
body: Bad news first: Furia Regia's two Thursday backs both beat their numbers — D'Andre Swift 19.0 (86% of Chicago's snaps, 26 of 28 back opportunities) and Rhamondre Stevenson 22.5 (5 for 93 and a touchdown) (RotoWire usage 22 Oct). ESPN now projects 145.2 to 122.8 and gives you 38%, down from 49%. George Pickens is still limited with the shoulder and plays Monday night.
Nothing you can do today changes that gap: the lineup is within 0.9 of the projection lineup, and the three open calls — Jacobs, Golden, Pickens — wait on Friday's and Saturday's reports.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Furia Regia still have Love, Jefferson, Lamb and McBride to play. You need Golden active against the defence that allows the second-most receiver points, Stroud against a Giants secondary missing Newsome and Edmunds, and Pickens on Monday.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Pickens listed doubtful or out on Saturday, or Golden inactive Sunday — the contingencies below decide both.

case.label: The player
case.body: Limited Thursday with a shoulder, his first appearance on Dallas's report this season (NBC Sports 22 Oct 20:46Z; PhillyVoice 22 Oct). The beat is not worried. Dallas play Monday night, after every bench player here has kicked off.

case.label: The timing
case.body: Dallas kick off Monday 18:15 CDMX. The lineup tool's check — inactives Monday 16:45 — would hand the slot to Rashee Rice, who is projected 0.0 and has kicked off by then anyway. Worthy (12.4) plays at Seattle Sunday 18:20, so Saturday's final Dallas report is the last useful information.

case.label: If Golden is out too
case.body: Worthy covers Golden's WR slot (that card is Sunday's 12:55 check), and the flex goes to whichever of Jacobs or Gordon is not starting at RB.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Saturday's Cowboys report lists Pickens doubtful or out → swap Worthy into the flex before Sun 18:20. Questionable after practising Friday and Saturday → keep Pickens: 13.3 against 12.4 is a coin flip the projection takes.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The swap is made and Pickens plays and outscores Worthy; or Pickens is kept on a questionable tag and is inactive Monday (archive).

whatWentWrong.title: The lineup tool's contingencies fire too late — twice this week
whatWentWrong.lead: Jacobs's check (Sun 12:55) comes after Gordon's 11:00 kickoff; Pickens's (Mon 16:45) hands the slot to Rice at 0.0.

case.label: What happened
case.body: lineup_check.py times every contingency from the questionable player's own kickoff. For Jacobs the fallback (Gordon) has already started; for Pickens, a Monday-night player, every bench body has played by Sunday 18:20 and its printed fallback is the injured Rice.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Both decisions move earlier: Jacobs only on a clear status by Sunday 10:30, Pickens on Saturday's report (the two cards above). Golden's contingency is fine — Worthy plays after Green Bay's inactives.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: ESPN's lock in this league is per-slot rather than per-player — it is not; a started player cannot be benched.

whatWentWrong.sources: lineup_check.py output · ESPN league file kickoffs

whatWentWrong.title: Week 6 was won with 9.9 left on the bench
whatWentWrong.lead: Stroud's 23.0 sat behind Daniels's 19.0; Worthy's 14.3 behind Garrett Wilson's 8.4.

case.label: The numbers
case.body: 150.8 to 88.62 over Los Cachanillas; best possible 160.7 (week-6 archive, recomputed this run).

case.label: The lesson
case.body: Both were projection calls that lost — no override, nothing to fix but to keep starting by projection, which is why Rice's card waits on practice rather than on a hunch.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: A projection-set Week 7 lineup leaves more than 15 points on the bench (archive).

worthALook.name: Colston Loveland
worthALook.lead: 12 targets Thursday, and Cole Kmet was carted off — decide on Tuesday.

case.label: The player
case.body: 7 for 69 and a touchdown on 12 targets, 83% of snaps and 69% of routes at home to New England (RotoWire usage 22 Oct) — after 5 and 7 touches the two weeks before (archive). Cole Kmet left in the fourth quarter with a right-knee injury; Ben Johnson: 'I don't think it looked very good', diagnosis due Friday (PFT 23 Oct).

case.label: Why here
case.body: Likely's Giants are on bye in Week 8 and IPADE's flex takes a tight end, so a second startable tight end has real value (STRATEGY §8). This is a starter-level need, not a patch — the bar for spending priority.

case.label: The cost
case.body: On waivers until Wed 28 Oct 01:00 CDMX; Bloodsports are 5th in an order that never resets — a claim drops you to last for the season. The named drop is Rashee Rice (no practice since Week 4, 0.0 projection) — above 50% owned, and dropping him disagrees with the market on the bet that his hamstring and knee keep him out.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Claim on Tuesday if Kmet's diagnosis is multi-week and Rice is inactive on Sunday night. Not before: the claim cannot process until Wednesday anyway, so waiting costs nothing and buys Friday's MRI and Sunday's inactives.
